name: Seated Cable Row with Wrist Cuffs
equipmentItems: Two load-rated wrist cuffs with attachment rings
grip: No hand-held grip. Hands stay relaxed; resistance connects through the wrist cuffs.
description: A low cable row in which cuffs carry the resistance instead of hand-held handles. The elbows travel toward the sides while the torso remains steady.
setup: Attach one cuff to each wrist using the cuff maker's fit and attachment instructions, then connect one low cable to each cuff.
Sit tall with feet braced, knees slightly bent and enough distance to begin with arms extended.
instructions: Begin with relaxed hands and gentle cable tension; keep the torso upright.
Pull the elbows back toward the lower ribs without leaning backward.
Finish with the upper arms near the torso and shoulder blades moving naturally.
Extend the arms slowly and repeat without letting the cables jerk the cuffs.
cues: Let the cuffs carry the load.
commonMistakes: Swinging backward to complete the row.
Gripping a handle or letting loose cuffs slide toward the hands.

logging.example: Two independent stacks each set to 15 kg: record 15 kg per side, with two stacks noted.
logging.note: Keep the same cable system. A shared-stack or single-cable rig is a different setup; pulley ratios affect resistance.

alternatives: Single-Arm Cable Row with Wrist Cuff
variantNote: Assumption: cuffs around the wrists, two low cables, close-elbow row. Upper-arm cuffs and a shared cable need their own variant instructions.
reviewNotes: Confirm cuff placement and whether your gym uses one cable or two.
General rowing references do not validate this specific cuff adaptation; trainer review pending.
